description: Make the DENY path of orch-agent-allowlist.sh fail closed when jq is absent, instead of fail-open (Task/Agent spawn proceeds).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: PreToolUse exit-code semantics: exit 0 + valid JSON stdout -> Claude processes permissionDecision (deny/allow/ask/defer); exit 2 -> blocking error, stdout ignored, stderr fed back, tool BLOCKED; other non-zero (e.g. 127 from a missing jq) -> non-blocking error, tool PROCEEDS (this is the fail-open). Therefore a static printf deny JSON + exit 0, or exit 2, both fail closed.

userStories.title: Add fail-closed jq-absence guard to the runtime hook + deny-without-jq test
userStories.description: As the cam capability gate, I need the runtime allowlist hook to emit a static deny (exit 0) when jq is absent, so that a missing jq denies every Task/Agent spawn instead of failing open and bypassing the whole gate.
acceptanceCriteria: In .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, AFTER the CAM_SESSION scope gate (line ~31-33) and AFTER the payload="$(cat)" read (line ~36), there is an early guard `if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... exit 0; fi` that prints a static deny JSON via printf (not via jq) when jq is unavailable. [oracle: grep -Eq 'command -v jq' .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]

The static deny JSON emitted by the printf guard is valid JSON with hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName="PreToolUse" and hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision="deny". [oracle: file-assert printf '{"tool_input":{"subagent_type":"x"}}' piped to the hook under a jq-free PATH parses as JSON with permissionDecision=="deny"; covered by the new test below]

The existing jq extraction read (line ~42-44), the ALLOW `case` block (line ~47-52), and the trailing `jq -n` deny emission (line ~55-68) remain byte-identical to the pre-change file (surgical: only the new guard and the header comment are added). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The hook header comment block (lines ~17-26) documents the fail-closed-without-jq behavior: when jq is absent the hook emits a static deny and exits 0, denying every spawn. [oracle: grep -Eq 'fail.?closed|denies every|static deny' .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]

A new test in test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts exercises the deny-without-jq path. Unlike every existing test (which uses test.skipIf(!jqAvailable)), this test RUNS even when jq IS present: it simulates jq-absence by spawning the hook with a restricted PATH that excludes jq (e.g. a mkdtemp dir symlinking only the binaries bash needs, like cat) and invoking via an absolute bash path (/bin/bash HOOK) so bash itself does not need PATH to be resolved. [oracle: grep -Eq 'command -v jq|jq-free|restricted PATH|without jq' test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
That new test asserts the result is a valid deny JSON (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision==="deny") AND exitCode===0. [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh (add guard + header comment), test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts (add one deny-without-jq test). Read scripts/cam/patterns.md bullets: 'PreToolUse deny contract + defensive subagent_type read (CAM-91)', 'Bun.spawn stdin/stdout pattern for shell-script integration tests (CAM-91)', 'CAM_SESSION scope-gate pattern for hooks (CAM-102)'. GOTCHA: existing tests skip when jq absent; the NEW test must do the OPPOSITE (run with jq present, simulate absence by spawning with a PATH that excludes jq). Spawn the hook via an absolute bash path (/bin/bash) so bash resolution does not depend on the restricted PATH; the restricted PATH only needs the binaries the hook uses before the guard (cat). The hook still needs CAM_SESSION set (scope gate) for the guard to be reached. Per Claude Code hooks spec (officialDocsConsulted): exit 0 + deny JSON = fail-closed; a missing jq otherwise exits 127 (non-blocking error) and the spawn PROCEEDS (fail-open). The static deny printf must produce the same hookSpecificOutput shape as the jq -n deny. patterns.md: append a bullet on fail-closed-without-jq if a durable insight emerges.
